subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared connected-Control-UI notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and how should cron snooze/reschedule actions be represented?
rationale: The remaining work is valid but crosses UI architecture, cron scheduling semantics, context UX, Web Push settings, WebChat actions, and admin notification security boundaries.

options.title: Scope core notification queue first
options.body: Define one connected-Control-UI notification/action contract, then implement cron-result and context-pressure integrations as separate focused changes.

options.title: Fold into related action work
options.body: Make the shared action/notification API canonical in a related tracker and keep this issue as UX requirements for that broader contract.

options.title: Defer in-app toasts
options.body: Keep the current inline cron, Web Push, and context-ring surfaces and close later only if maintainers reject a core toast/snooze layer.

recommendation.title: Scope core notification queue first
recommendation.body: Define one connected-Control-UI notification/action contract, then implement cron-result and context-pressure integrations as separate focused changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has prior review context on this issue and recent history in cron notification routing and product-boundary decisions around this surface.
